intro: Riggers plan and move heavy loads safely, skills used across construction, mining and manufacturing. The closest of the 25 careers below is Hoist and Winch Operators, with an 88% match, while Boilermakers are 77% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $76,410, which is 22% more than the $62,640 riggers earn.
why_it_works: Every lift means calculating weights, choosing slings and signals and coordinating with crane operators so nobody gets hurt. O*NET rates operation and control at 3.25 out of 5 for riggers, and operations monitoring and coordination at 3.12. Ironwork, aircraft assembly and equipment operation use the same skills. Almost all matches need no extra schooling. The gaps are training others and maintenance.
tips: Structural Iron and Steel Workers earn $62,780, about the same, and use your rigging daily.
Mining roof bolters earn $78,540, which is 25% more, and are a 78% match.
A crane operator certification builds on rigging and raises your pay range.

faq.q: What jobs can former riggers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Hoist and Winch Operators (88%), surface mining excavating operators (84%) and Structural Iron and Steel Workers (84%), based on O*NET 31.0. Aircraft structure and rigging assemblers are 83% matched and earn $65,380, which is 4% more than the $62,640 rigger median.

faq.q: Which careers for riggers pay more?
faq.a: 10 of the 25 matches pay more. Mining roof bolters earn $78,540 (25% more), Boilermakers $76,410 (22% more) and Terrazzo Workers and Finishers $76,170 (22% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Most train through apprenticeships or on the job.

faq.q: Do riggers need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than riggers already have, including 8 of the top 10. In a close match, 71% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and a certification can help.

The skills that most often need work are operations monitoring, instructing, operation and control and equipment maintenance. Complex problem solving already rates 3 out of 5 for riggers in O*NET, so running equipment and training crews are the main steps toward better pay.
